name: Jay Choi
episode: The missing name on the stern
life: “I still remember mixing the right color before understanding the lettering.” Thursday often includes a stop at the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, where Jay can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I transposed two letters in my first language and put the brush down when I saw the owner seeing it.
appearance: Back on the street, look for a boxy denim jacket and a small enamel bird on the lapel. Jay has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, with short black hair swept back. Jay starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak during a conversation.
personality: Jay finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To acknowledge the spelling error to its owners.
family: Leon Mehta is Jay’s older cousin. Jay is free to hang up first. Leon makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The hair after illness*, Leon says, “I sold her the wig. I want to help her give it away without telling the next owner its history.”
connections: Shay Gray (skipper). The apprentice and the old skipper can admit the error without losing the family's preferred spelling.
